findings.title: service_account inherits full internal-user access
findings.problem: User.is_external_user only compares user_type to config.EXTERNAL_USER_TYPE ('external'), so the newly-accepted 'service_account' value never satisfies it. Every downstream authorization check that branches on is_external_user instead of an explicit service-account check therefore treats a service account exactly like a regular internal human user, with no policy decision behind it.
findings.impact: Verified at three live consumers: LLM/embedding model access (src/codemie/service/llm_service/llm_service.py:340, get_allowed_models: 'if not user.is_external_user: return all models') grants a service account unrestricted model access; marketplace assistant visibility (src/codemie/rest_api/models/assistant.py:849, Assistant.is_shared_with, and src/codemie/service/assistant/assistant_repository.py:526, _get_marketplace_condition) grants full, unrestricted visibility into every global assistant. Neither the ticket nor the spec defines the intended privilege scope for a non-interactive/service credential, so this ships a real access-scope outcome by default rather than by decision.
findings.recommendation: Get explicit product/security sign-off on the intended access scope for service_account (LLM/model access, marketplace visibility, project scope), then encode it explicitly (e.g. an is_service_account check or dedicated branch) rather than relying on the absence of is_external_user.

findings.title: 401 error text omits service_account from valid values
findings.problem: validate_user_type's rejection paths (the invalid-type branch and the invalid-value branch at lines 93-104) still hardcode "Expected 'regular' or 'external'" / "Only 'regular' and 'external' are supported", unchanged even though VALID_USER_TYPES now has three members. The same stale text is re-wrapped verbatim in src/codemie/enterprise/idp/dependencies.py:120 when an enterprise IDP's InvalidUserTypeError is caught and re-raised as an ExtendedHTTPException.
findings.impact: An admin troubleshooting a 401 from a mistyped or misconfigured IDP user_type claim is told only two values are valid, hiding that 'service_account' is now supported. tests/codemie/rest_api/security/test_user_type_validator.py pins this stale substring, so the drift cannot be caught by the existing suite.
findings.recommendation: Build the message/details text from sorted(VALID_USER_TYPES) in both branches of user_type_validator.py, and in the wrapping message in enterprise/idp/dependencies.py, instead of a hardcoded 'regular'/'external' literal.

findings.title: Admin user_type update API rejects service_account
findings.problem: UserManagementService._validate_user_type - used by update_user_fields, the local-mode admin user-management API - has its own independent hardcoded check 'if normalized not in ["regular", "external"]', never updated to include 'service_account' and never wired to the VALID_USER_TYPES constant this ticket extended in user_type_validator.py.
findings.impact: An admin cannot manually set or correct a user's user_type to 'service_account' via the local-mode admin API (400 'Invalid user_type'), even though IDP-based first-login provisioning can now create such a user - an inconsistent, asymmetric contract for the exact field this ticket changed.
findings.recommendation: Import/reuse VALID_USER_TYPES from user_type_validator.py in _validate_user_type instead of a separately hardcoded list.

findings.title: InvalidUserTypeError detail omits service_account
findings.problem: validate_user_type's invalid-value branch still raises InvalidUserTypeError with detail/log text hardcoded to 'regular'/'external' ("...not recognized. Only 'regular' and 'external' are supported."), unchanged despite VALID_USER_TYPES gaining 'service_account' two lines above in the same file.
findings.impact: The stale detail string reaches the end-user 401 response via codemie's dependencies.py wrapper, telling an admin fixing an enterprise IDP (Keycloak/OIDC/EntraID) misconfiguration that only two values are supported.
findings.recommendation: Derive the detail/log text from sorted(VALID_USER_TYPES) so it stays accurate as the set grows.

findings.title: No direct unit test for enterprise validate_user_type normalization
findings.problem: Unlike the base repo, which added 3 direct unit tests against validate_user_type for 'service_account' (lowercase/uppercase/whitespace-trimmed), the enterprise repo adds no equivalent direct test; no test in tests/ calls validate_user_type at all. Coverage is only indirect, through KeycloakIdpProvider.authenticate and the admin-user attribute parser, both exercised with the literal lowercase 'service_account' only - never uppercase or whitespace-padded input.
findings.impact: A future change to the enterprise validator's normalization (or an accidental divergence from the base repo's implementation) could silently pass its indirect test suite while breaking case-insensitive/whitespace handling for this new value.
findings.recommendation: Add direct unit tests for src/codemie_enterprise/idp/user_type.py's validate_user_type mirroring the base repo's lowercase/uppercase/whitespace-trimmed cases for 'service_account'.
